body.statement: Within the retained-variable response language, exogenous sources having the same nonempty child set can be merged without changing any structural solution, giving at most \(H_{\max}=2^N-1\) independent sources.  Every permitted finite architecture embeds in the saturated super-architecture for its topological order by making added directed inputs inessential and unused sources degenerate; hence at most \(A_{\max}=N!\) super-architectures suffice.  On any fixed permitted architecture, sourcewise barycentric reduction preserves \(\zeta(M)\) with at most \(K_{\max}=m+3\) values per source, and the resulting dense table system is counted by \(R_{\max}\).  Every point of \(\mathfrak F_\delta(\mathcal P,q)\) induces an SCM in \(\mathfrak M_\delta(\mathcal P,q)\), and the image of \(\mathfrak F_\delta(\mathcal P,q)\) is exactly the target-value set of the enumerated bounded finite SCMs satisfying actual selected-MAG legality.  Neither barycentric reduction nor saturated embedding is asserted to give a graph-legal equal-moment representative for every arbitrary admissible SCM.
body.justification: The compiler gives a maximal finite response language with one saturated super-architecture per order while keeping moment reduction logically separate from graph-legal lifting.
body.gap: The source-merging and barycentric components are informed by Evans, Rosset, Gisin, and Wolfe, and Duarte et al.; their results do not preserve strict functional-essentiality witnesses under support deletion.
body.consumer: It supplies an auditable candidate model language for the Lee et al. FCI and LV-IDA setting without treating the candidate language as the full SCM class.
body.proof_tex:
We use the corrected saturated architecture list.  First consider a permitted recursive response architecture on the retained vertices.  Group its mutually independent exogenous sources by their nonempty retained child sets.  For each \(\varnothing\ne C\subseteq W\), let \(U_C\) be the tuple of all original sources having child set \(C\), with the product law inherited from those sources.  Tuples associated with distinct child sets have disjoint original coordinates and therefore remain mutually independent.  Substitute the tuple coordinates into the old structural equations.  For every exogenous realization and every hard intervention, recursive evaluation in topological order gives exactly the old endogenous solution.  Thus \((V,S)\), \((A^b,S^b)\), and every coordinate of \(\zeta(M)\) are unchanged.  An equation depends essentially on the tuple \(U_C\) if and only if it depends essentially on at least one coordinate: one implication follows by changing that coordinate, while for the other one changes two tuples one coordinate at a time and takes the first step at which the output changes.  Hence the minimal structural graph is unchanged.  Sources with no retained child may be discarded.  There are \(2^N-1=H_{\max}\) nonempty subsets of \(W\), which proves the source-count bound within this response language.

Fix a topological order \(\prec\) for any current permitted finite architecture.  Its saturated super-architecture \(T_{\prec}\) contains every old directed input and every old child-set source.  Define each dense response table to ignore every newly added endogenous input.  For a child set absent from the old architecture, give \(U_C\) a one-point law and make every incident table ignore it; for a child set present in the old architecture, retain its law and its old table dependence.  Induction in the order \(\prec\) shows that the structural solution is unchanged under every intervention.  Moreover, each added directed feature and each unused source feature has essentiality polynomial zero, while every old essential feature retains its old positive witness.  By \(\text{lem:essential-feature-iff}\), the actual minimal graph and its selected projection are unchanged.  Thus every old architecture embeds in one saturated architecture indexed only by its order.  There are at most \(N!=A_{\max}\) orders.

We next prove moment reduction.  After source merging, write the independent sources as \(U_1,\ldots,U_H\), where \(H\le H_{\max}\), and define
\[
 F(U_1,\ldots,U_H)=
 \left(
   (\mathbf 1\{V=v,S=1\})_{v\in\Omega_V},
   h(A^b)\mathbf 1\{S^b=1\},
   \mathbf 1\{S^b=1\}
 \right)\in\mathbb R^{m+2}.
\]
By \(\text{def:moment-map}\), \(\mathbb E[F]=\zeta(M)\).  Hold all source laws except that of \(U_k\) fixed, and put
\[
 g_k(u)=\int F(u_1,\ldots,u_{k-1},u,u_{k+1},\ldots,u_H)
             \prod_{r\ne k}dP_r(u_r).
\]
Independence and iterated integration give
\[
 \zeta(M)=\int g_k(u)\,dP_k(u).
\]

We record the elementary barycenter argument used here.  If an integrable random vector \(Y\) takes values in \(\mathbb R^d\), its expectation belongs to the convex hull of at most \(d+1\) values in the essential range of \(Y\).  Indeed, separation places the expectation in the closed convex hull of the essential range.  If it lies on a proper supporting hyperplane, the nonnegative difference between the supporting affine functional and its boundary value has expectation zero and hence vanishes almost surely; restricting to that hyperplane lowers the affine dimension.  Iteration reaches the relative interior of the closed convex hull in the resulting affine space, which is contained in the convex hull itself.  A finite convex representation then exists, and any representation with more than \(d+1\) points has an affine dependence.  Moving its coefficients along that dependence until one coefficient vanishes preserves both their sum and the barycenter.  Repetition leaves at most \(d+1\) points.

Apply this argument with \(d=m+2\) to \(g_k(U_k)\).  There are values \(u_{k,1},\ldots,u_{k,L_k}\), nonnegative weights \(w_{k,r}\), and \(L_k\le m+3=K_{\max}\) such that
\[
 \sum_{r=1}^{L_k}w_{k,r}=1,
 \qquad
 \sum_{r=1}^{L_k}w_{k,r}g_k(u_{k,r})
 =\int g_k(u)\,dP_k(u).
\]
Replacing only \(P_k\) by this discrete law preserves \(\zeta(M)\) and product factorization.  Repeat for \(k=1,\ldots,H\), always using the currently installed laws for the other sources.  Each step preserves the same full vector, so the final vector remains \(\zeta(M)\), and each source has at most \(K_{\max}\) values.  In particular, the shared normalization
\[
 \rho=\sum_{v\in\Omega_V}c_v(M)
\]
is preserved.  After embedding in the saturated order, zero-mass slots pad every source to \(K_{\max}\), and the finite dense table system is among those counted by the corrected \(R_{\max}\).  This reduction preserves moments; it need not preserve a strict inequality \(Z_e>0\).

Finally take \((p_T,\rho)\in\mathfrak F_\delta(\mathcal P,q)\).  A saturated topological order, its deterministic tables, and its mutually independent source-simplex laws define a recursive finite SCM \(M_{T,p_T}\).  The graph-legality stratum gives a \(G\in\mathcal G(\mathcal P)\) with \(\Psi_{T,G}(p_T)\); hence \(\text{lem:essential-feature-iff}\) yields
\[
 G_S(M_{T,p_T})=G.
\]
The remaining fiber constraints give, for every \(v\in\Omega_V\),
\[
 c_v(M_{T,p_T})=\Phi_T(p_T)_{c_v}=\rho q(v),
 \qquad \delta\le\rho\le1,
 \qquad d_{M_{T,p_T}}=\Phi_T(p_T)_d\ge\delta.
\]
Together with \(\text{ass:positive-selected-law}\), these are the member conditions in \(\text{def:admissible-class}\), so \(M_{T,p_T}\in\mathfrak M_\delta(\mathcal P,q)\).  Because \(\delta>0\), division in
\[
 \theta(M_{T,p_T})=\frac{\Phi_T(p_T)_n}{\Phi_T(p_T)_d}
\]
is valid.

Conversely, an enumerated bounded finite SCM satisfying actual selected-MAG legality has a listed order, a listed dense table system, product source masses \(p_T\), and \(\rho=\sum_v c_v\).  Its exact graph sign pattern satisfies one \(\Psi_{T,G}\) by \(\text{lem:essential-feature-iff}\), and selected-law fit plus the two margins place \((p_T,\rho)\) in \(\mathfrak F_\delta(\mathcal P,q)\).  The two inclusions prove the asserted equality of images.  Nothing in this argument turns moment preservation into preservation of strict essentiality, or exogenizes arbitrary latent endogenous structure while preserving actual parent semantics; those are precisely the unresolved legal-lifting issues.
